Episode 145. Prologue (11)
Meanwhile, Tallaris was watching Ron from the deepest part of the castle.
Ron's breath was so faint that even Tallaris had to concentrate to hear it. It was weaker than the day she first visited.
The robust body of the Sword Emperor looked emaciated, unable to be concealed by clothes and blankets, and the air was filled with the thick scent of death.
"Ron."
Tallaris sat on the bed and carefully held Ron's dry hand.
"Your grandson you love so much, his friend, and your knights are all fighting for Hiran. Aren't you really going to wake up?"
The only two people Tallaris could call friends.
Siron Runkandel and Ron Hiran. Tallaris shook her head, recalling their old images.
"Ah, these pathetic humans. The stronger you get, the more you disappoint me."
The fact that Kelliac Zhipul could come in person was of course already anticipated by many, but facing his majesty directly, people felt a breath-taking sensation.
The fleet was obscured by the power of flames. The flagship at the forefront, Kozheg, was so far away that it was the size of a finger.
Yet everyone in the Sword Emperor City felt as if they were facing Kelliac one step ahead.
The overwhelming presence, the fleet led by the world's top leader, was slowly approaching the Sword Emperor City.
Among the knights of the Sword Emperor City, not a single one feared death.
But also, there was not a single person who thought they could fight and win against them. It seemed like no miracles or unexpected events could occur.
Morale was not dropping.
They were just a little worried. Even if they couldn't win, they could end without even a meaningful counterattack.
"Finally, I'm going to see the face of the current Zhipul family head."
Murakan spoke in a low voice.
This was the first time Jin had seen Kelliac Zhipul in person. In his previous life and in his current life, he had only seen him through newsletters and family documents.
"He's a big shot. I'm curious to see what he's like in person."
Fortunately, Zhipul's main force did not attack the Sword Emperor City as soon as they appeared. The problem that Amela was worried about did not occur.
The current Kozheg could radiate a power on a different scale from what Jin had experienced before.
"Lady Luyan."
"Speak, Sir Jin."
"I suppose Runkandel has also finished preparing for a full-scale war."
"I would guess so. If Zhipul is showing off like that, Runkandel can't just sit still. If Runkandel steps forward, some of Hiran might survive...."
"Not some. We will save them all."
"If you're sincere, and have the ability, I know. But we will never run away when it comes to the small family head."
"I feel the same, Lady Luyan. However, I would like to make one promise with you."
"A promise?"
"The seal of chaos that trapped Dante happened because he was resisting chaos."
Jin informed Luyan that Tallaris was here.
She had given him permission to tell Luyan more about the mission of the Abyss and the dangers of chaos earlier. It was because Tallaris allowed it, not for Luyan, but for Jin.
For a while, Jin explained the stories about it, and Luyan listened carefully.
"...So, if the small family head can't overcome the power of the white stone, a monster that even the Abyss Lord can't handle alone awakens?"
"That's right."
"So, how does the small family head... Ah."
Luyan didn't question why they were having this conversation now.

She knew that it was thanks to Jin being at the center of this incident that the Abyss Lord was considering the situation even while revealing the mission of the Abyss to outsiders. And even if Jin had warned in advance, the situation wouldn't have changed.
"...If such a thing happens, promise me that you will retreat all the remaining Hiran knights."

If Dante dies and chaos awakens, and if the Sword Emperor's Palace becomes a battleground between Zhipul and Runkandel or a chaos extermination battleground, it would be right for the Hiran knights to leave.
Whether they get swept away and die in the war of the two great families, or die to the monster of chaos. It would be nothing but a dog's death.
In that case, chaos would have killed Dante, and they would have to fight to take revenge on the monster.
Luyan couldn't bring herself to say that. She understood what Jin's feelings were asking for such a promise.
Considering Dante's death was in itself a heart-wrenching thing for Jin.
"...I will do so."
Luyan replied in a dark voice.
The fate that befell Hiran was unjust.
Despite staking their lives to protect Dante and Hiran's pride, Hiran could only exist if the chaos of the white stone devoured Dante and awakened. A miserable and terrifying existence.
"In return, make me one promise as well."
"Speak."
"If by chance, the small family head comes back... If he comes back when we're gone. Please help Dante not to become a monster."
No one knew how the situation would develop.
Luyan was talking about a situation where Dante survived alone and Hiran was destroyed.
She was asking for help to prevent Dante from losing his way and becoming a demon, kneeled by loss, sorrow, and wounds.
Here is the English translation of the provided text:
Only a friend can help in such a situation.
"Dante has already suffered too much. It must have been hard for him. Even now."
"Even if Dante falls into hatred and lashes out at me, I won't let go of Dante."
"Yes, you are the person to do that. I just wanted to say something. Because there's so little Hyran can do for that kid."
The flames of Kelliac now dyed the Imperial City red, and the fleet stopped advancing. Those on the wall all looked up and glared at the fleet.
Between the magicians standing at the forefront of the Cojek, an old man with long white hair and a white robe was coming out.
It was Kelliac Jipl.
"Spread the barrier!"
The commander of the Dragon Knight Brigade, Calmain, cried out with his eyes wide open.
This was because the heat extending from the flames enveloping the fleet was already infiltrating the entire Imperial City. The heat was unbearable even for the normal knights.
The stones forming the wall were turning red, radiating heat, and the air was so hot it seemed to melt the lungs and organs.
Nobody expected this.
It wasn't as if a proper magic had been deployed yet, nor was the whole fleet moving, it was a phenomenon that happened just because Kelliac alone came to the front of the Cojek.
The knights spread the barrier and activated the defense equipment. It seemed as if the entire Imperial City was covered with a blue shield in an instant, blocking the heat.
But the next moment, when Kelliac swung the Jipl family's exclusive staff 'Huroti' once, the barrier that had been surrounding the Imperial City disappeared.
As if it had never been spread in the first place.
"I just came to have a chat because I was curious about someone, don't overreact."
"You dare to say nonsense after spewing fire that could melt the fortress."
At Calmain's words, Kelliac smiled softly, like a gentle old man indulging a tantrum-throwing child.
"Ah, it's been a while since I've been on a battlefield, so I didn't pay attention to that. I'll put it away."

As soon as he finished speaking, the heat disappeared as if it was a lie. The power of the flame still engulfed the fleet, indicating that Kelliac's power clearly reached beyond magic, into the realm of divine power.
"And, just to remind you, don't interrupt my conversation any further. If I wanted to, I could annihilate you all in a few seconds. Show me the same consideration that I've shown you."
"Kelliac...! How much do you intend to belittle us!"
The one who yelled was Commander Goro, who was standing on the left side of the wall. He had evacuated non-combat personnel and civilians during the first battle.
He didn't yell with any particular intention.
He was just unconsciously venting his resistance to the overwhelming pressure and fear that bound his whole body.
"You are hard of hearing."
Those who had reached the state of a warrior could now see what was about to happen. However, they had no means to stop it and no time to warn of the danger.
Also, their intuition was wrong.
Thump
Space explosion.
Kelliac Ziphil's magic unfolded.
However, the target was not Golo. Everyone thought Golo would explode and die, but Kelliac's magic destroyed Kalmain Aita.
An explosion occurred on Kalmain's shoulder.

The explosion completely took away Kalmain's right arm. The right arm, ripped and bounced by the explosion, was scattered without a trace by the subsequent space explosion. Only the futile sound of the sword falling on the stone floor remained.
"Cough...!"
"Commander!"
"Kalmain!"

The Dragon Knights and Sword Saints shouted simultaneously and tried to approach Kalmain. But Kelliac stopped their movement by triggering space explosions right in front of their faces, as if a final warning.
Then he said this.
"My consideration ends here."
Most of those in Sword Emperor City did not recall hearing a more chilling voice in their lives.
A frightfully sudden silence ensued. Kelliac waited for about five seconds, checked that no one was moving, and met Jin's gaze. He wore an indescribably kind smile.
'Jin Runcandel.'
'Kelliac Ziphil.'
Faced with the majesty in Kelliac's eyes, Jin felt his blood chill and his joints ache. He had an aura that was completely different from the transcendent individuals Jin had encountered so far.
Soft yet strong, dark yet sharp, light yet heavy, gentle yet evil.
Jin defined the sensation of the person called Kelliac Ziphil like this.
'I see why people who have seen Kelliac in person compare him to a god.'
Undoubtedly, he was an indescribably shocking character.
'But, I understand why Kelliac is the second in command.'
Jin saw through the reason Kelliac stood behind Siron, seeing the odd divine aura of Kelliac, and the single emotion hidden in that smile.
So, Jin also gave him a smile.
"You hate me, don't you, Sir Kelliac Ziphil."
If the person in front of him was Siron and not Kelliac, Jin would never have been able to read his emotions.

In the first place, his father was a being who would never harbor such a profoundly human emotion as hatred toward him. No matter how Jin provoked him, his father would never hold any emotion greater than anger.
Even if he had been born a Ziphil and killed everyone in Runcandel.
"Did it show?"
Kelliac asked in a calm voice.
"Yes, it made your divine power seem dim."
Jin responded, erasing his smile.
